title: EventBridge Rule Invocation and Failed Invocations

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch` events with `namespace="AWS/Events" metric_name="FailedInvocations"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.38 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch` traffic without `namespace="AWS/Events" metric_name="FailedInvocations"`. Confirm UC-4.1.38 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Events" metric_name="FailedInvocations"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.38_eventbridge_rule_invocat_38"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.38 — EventBridge Rule Invocation and Failed Invocations: queries AWS `aws:cloudwatch` for search criteria `namespace="AWS/Events" metric_name="FailedInvocations"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'EventBridge Rule Invocation and Failed Invocations' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.38 drives medium-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Collect EventBridge metrics per rule. Alert on FailedInvocations > 0. Correlate with target service (e.g. Lambda errors, SQS rejections) for root cause.
visualization: Table (rule, failures), Line chart (invocations vs failures), Single value.

dataModelAcceleration: Change: EventBridge failed invocations when mapped to All_Changes; else keep Step 2 on CloudWatch `AWS/Events`. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. knownFalsePositives: Rules pointed at throttled or sleeping targets, deploy windows, and canary invocations in non-production.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect EventBridge metrics per rule. Alert on FailedInvocations > 0. Correlate with target service (e.g. Lambda errors, SQS rejections) for root cause.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Events" metric_name="FailedInvocations"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.38_eventbridge_rule_invocat_38"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect eventbridge rule invocation and failed invocations. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_38_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (rule, failures), Line chart (invocations vs failures), Single value..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of eventbridge rule invocation and failed invocations so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
